subject: How to get the "W" matrix from "WLS"?

messages.author: e3cd7ac95409208e
messages.subject: How to get the "W" matrix from "WLS"?
parts:
Hello lavaan users! For one reason or another I see myself needing to learn how to obtain in R the matrix of fourth-order moments. So far, all I have been able to find are R packages or functions that calculate univariate kurtosis, but not the matrix itself.

Then I remembered that Asymptotic Distribution Free estimator (which I believe in lavaan is called "WLS") calculates this matrix as part of the estimator.

Is there a way to extract it from the output? Is it stored somewhere?

Or does anyone have a suggestion about how to calculate the matrix of fourth order moments in R?

Thank you!

- Elia

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How to get the "W" matrix from "WLS"?
parts: Is there a way to extract it from the output? Is it stored somewhere?

It might be stored somewhere in the lavaan object, I don't see "fourth-order moments" explicitly listed on the ?lavInspect help page.  Perhaps it is the "wls.v" option, if the weight matrix is indeed the matrix of fourth-order moments.
Or does anyone have a suggestion about how to calculate the matrix of fourth order moments in R?

Someone posted a function for calculating co-kurtosis here:  https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-finance/2006q3/000977.html
But it is just for one pair of variables at a time, so you'd have to use it iteratively.  At the very least, you could use it to check a couple numbers from the lavInspect(fit, "wls.v") output to check whether that is indeed the matrix you want.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: How to get the "W" matrix from "WLS"?
parts:
On 08/26/2016 09:02 AM, Elia Emmers wrote:
> Is there a way to extract it from the output? Is it stored somewhere?

lavInspect(fit, "WLS.V") will give you the 'W' matrix. When estimator =
"WLS", this is a full matrix, where the elements are the inverse of the
asymptotic variance matrix of the sample statistics.

> Or does anyone have a suggestion about how to calculate the matrix of
> fourth order moments in R?

I think you are looking for the 'Gamma' matrix, which is N times the
asymptotic variance matrix of the sample statistics. You can get it from

lavInspect(fit, "gamma")

To see how this matrix is computed, have a look at the function
lav_samplestats_Gamma() in the file lav_samplestats_gamma.R in the
lavaan source code.

Yves.
